name: Schools & Education
eyebrow: Automation for schools, colleges, coaching institutes and EdTech teams
headline: Every enquiry answered, every parent informed, more time to teach.
summary: MoreSpace builds consented WhatsApp, ERP and LMS workflows for admissions, attendance and bus alerts, fees, results and learner support. AI drafts, sorts and summarizes; counselors, teachers and principals decide every admission, grade, concession and disciplinary matter.
shareText: How MoreSpace automates admissions, parent updates, fees and learner support for schools, colleges, coaching institutes and EdTech, with educators deciding what matters.
audience: College registrars, deans of students and examination controllers
Coaching institute founders, center heads and academic coordinators
EdTech founders, growth leads and learner success teams
IT heads, accounts officers and data protection contacts

challenges.title: Admission enquiries leak between ads, calls and walk-ins
challenges.description: Leads arrive from Meta and Google forms, the website, education fairs, walk-ins and WhatsApp, often after office hours. Counselors work from personal phones and spreadsheets, follow-ups slip in peak season, and nobody can say which campaign actually filled seats.

challenges.title: Parents get many messages and still miss the important ones
challenges.description: Circulars, homework, fee notices and photos land in crowded class groups. A same-day absence or a delayed bus is easily lost, and the school cannot tell who has read a trip consent slip or a safety notice.

challenges.title: Teachers spend evenings on administration
challenges.description: Substitution plans, attendance registers, report card remarks, PTM scheduling and repeated parent questions eat into teaching and preparation time, and the extra work falls unevenly across staff.

challenges.title: Fee follow-up strains relationships
challenges.description: Chasing dues by phone is slow and awkward, reminders sometimes reach the wrong person or a class group, and installment, concession and refund requests get lost between the front office and accounts.

challenges.title: Learners drift away before anyone notices
challenges.description: Coaching students fall behind after a few weak tests and doubts that never get answered, and online learners stop after the first modules. By the time a mentor notices, the learner has disengaged or asked for a refund.

challenges.title: Children's data and advertising rules are tightening
challenges.description: From May 2027 the DPDP Act and Rules require verifiable parental consent for anyone under eighteen and restrict tracking and targeted advertising, while coaching, consumer and UGC rules already add duties on claims, refunds and grievances. Class groups and spreadsheets do not meet them.

flagship.title: One admissions pipeline from first enquiry to confirmed seat
flagship.summary: Every enquiry, whether from an ad, the website, a fair, a walk-in or WhatsApp, lands in one CRM with its source, gets an instant acknowledgment and a named counselor, and moves through campus visit or demo, application, document check and fee payment without falling between teams. Answers come only from the approved prospectus and fee schedule, and the admissions head sees the funnel by program and campaign.

steps.title: Capture every enquiry with its source
steps.description: Meta and Google lead forms, website forms, fair QR codes and walk-in tablets feed one CRM record per family, de-duplicated by phone number, with campaign, program or grade, campus, consent and notice version recorded at capture.

steps.title: Acknowledge and assign within minutes
steps.description: An approved WhatsApp template thanks the family, shares the prospectus link and names the counselor, assigned by program, campus and language. Leads with no counselor contact in the agreed time escalate to the admissions head.

steps.title: Answer from approved content only
steps.description: Questions on fees, transport, dates, eligibility and documents are answered from the prospectus, fee schedule and admissions calendar the institution approves, citing the source. Anything else, or anything the model is unsure about, goes to the counselor.

steps.title: Book the visit, demo or counseling call
steps.description: Families pick a campus tour, open-day slot, demo class or counselor call from live calendars, receive reminders with directions and reschedule in one tap. The counselor records the outcome after every visit.

steps.title: Collect the application and documents
steps.description: A secure application link pre-fills known details and lists the documents each program needs. Uploads are checked for completeness and readability, and missing items trigger polite reminders until the admissions office verifies the file.

steps.title: Confirm the seat and report the funnel
steps.description: After the admissions office approves, the family receives the offer and fee link, the record moves into the ERP, and a daily dashboard shows enquiries, visits, applications and confirmed seats by program, campus and campaign.

flagship.humanCheckpoint: Counselors own every family conversation. The admissions head approves templates, answer content and routing before launch, and only the admissions office decides eligibility, concessions and offers. The automation never screens or ranks children or parents, and RTE entry-level seats follow the state's own process.
outcomes: Faster first responses to enquiries, including evenings and weekends
Fewer families lost between enquiry, visit and application
Counselor time goes to conversations instead of data entry and chasing
Admissions spend judged by confirmed seats, not just leads

stages.title: Discover and enquire
stages.description: Parents and students compare institutions on search, social media, review sites and word of mouth, then enquire by form, call, WhatsApp or walk-in, often in the evening and within a short admissions season.

stages.title: Visit, demo or trial
stages.description: Families tour the campus or attend an open day, aspirants sit a demo class, and online learners try a course before paying. Most enrollment decisions are made here, and slow follow-up loses them.

stages.title: Apply and enroll
stages.description: Applications, document checks, eligibility and counseling rounds, offers and the first fee payment. Missing documents and unclear fee or refund terms are the usual reasons a willing family stalls.

stages.title: Onboard and schedule
stages.description: New students receive batches or sections, timetables, LMS logins, transport routes and orientation details. Changes in the first weeks are frequent, and each one has to reach the right student and parent.

stages.title: Attend and learn
stages.description: Daily classes, attendance, bus journeys, homework, circulars, substitutions and questions to the office. Communication volume is highest here, and this is where safety and well-being concerns first appear.
stages.owner: Principal, academic head or learner success lead

stages.title: Assess and report
stages.description: Unit tests, mock tests, semester exams, report cards and parent-teacher meetings. Results have to reach families accurately and privately, and a weak result needs a mentor's attention, not just a number.

stages.title: Pay, renew and stay connected
stages.description: Term fees and installments, re-enrollment for the next year or course, graduation and transcripts, and alumni ties that bring referrals, mentoring and placements.
stages.owner: Accounts officer and alumni relations lead

segments.name: K-12 schools
segments.headline: Calmer admissions, safer school days and parents who hear what matters
segments.summary: K-12 schools talk to hundreds of families a day about admissions, attendance, buses, homework, fees and results. We connect the school ERP to one opted-in WhatsApp number and staff dashboards, so parents get timely, private updates, teachers lose repetitive admin and the principal can see what was sent, read and escalated.
challenges: Admission season brings a flood of enquiries and campus tour requests that the front office handles by phone, with little follow-up once the call ends.
Absence and bus updates depend on a teacher or the transport in-charge finding time to call, so a child who did not arrive may not be noticed quickly.
Class WhatsApp groups mix circulars, homework and chatter, expose parents' numbers to each other and leave no record of who read a safety notice.
Daily substitutions are planned on paper before assembly, and the same willing teachers absorb most of the extra periods.
Fee follow-up by phone and noticeboard is slow and awkward, and can embarrass children when dues are raised in class.

uses.title: Enquiry-to-tour admissions desk
uses.description: Enquiries from ads, the website and walk-ins logged with their source, answered from the approved prospectus, and moved to a campus tour with reminders and counselor follow-up.

uses.title: Same-day absence alerts
uses.description: Students marked absent without approved leave trigger a private message to the parent by mid-morning, with reply buttons. Parents who did not know get a call from the class teacher or coordinator.

uses.title: Bus boarding, drop and delay updates
uses.description: Boarding and drop events from bus RFID readers or the attendant's app notify the parent, and route delays are announced only after the transport in-charge approves the message.

uses.title: One channel for circulars, homework and PTMs
uses.description: Teacher-approved homework digests and circulars per child, translations checked by a fluent teacher, acknowledgment tracking for consent slips, and PTM slot booking from teachers' calendars.

uses.title: Substitution plans before the first bell
uses.description: A fair substitution plan proposed from the timetable and leave records, approved by the vice-principal and sent to substitutes with the absent teacher's lesson notes.

uses.title: Private fee reminders and secure report cards
uses.description: Courteous reminders and instant receipts sent only to the fee payer, and report cards released behind secure links once the principal locks results.

kpis: Parents notified of unexplained absence by the agreed time
Substitution plans published before first period
systems: School ERP such as Entab CampusCare, Fedena or Teachmint
GPS and RFID school bus tracking
Payment gateway with UPI and automatic receipts

segments.name: Colleges & universities
segments.headline: From application season to alumni, without the paperwork chase
segments.summary: Colleges and universities juggle thousands of applicants, many programs, counseling rounds, hostels and student services. We connect the admissions CRM, college ERP and student channels so applicants know what is missing, students get handbook answers at any hour, and grievances, ragging reports and distress reach the right committee or counselor.
challenges: Applicants submit incomplete or unreadable documents across several counseling rounds, and admissions staff chase them one call at a time.
Withdrawals and refunds have to follow the UGC fee refund policy, and original certificates may be verified and returned but never retained.
The same questions about hostel rules, exam forms, scholarships and timetables reach department offices hundreds of times a term.
Grievances, ragging complaints and signs of distress need a fast, recorded route to the right committee or counselor, not a shared inbox.
Alumni records go stale after graduation, so mentoring, placements and giving depend on a few personal networks.

uses.title: Program-wise enquiry routing
uses.description: Enquiries tagged by program, campus and entrance exam, assigned to the right counselor and followed up with approved content through each counseling round.

uses.title: Document checklist and verification queue
uses.description: Program and category checklists, readability and name-match checks on uploads, and a verification queue for the admissions office, with originals verified in person and returned the same day.

uses.title: Handbook and policy helpdesk
uses.description: Students and parents ask about hostel rules, exam forms, scholarships and fees and get answers cited from the current handbook, with anything personal or sensitive handed to staff.

uses.title: Committee-routed concerns
uses.description: Grievances go to the Students' Grievance Redressal Committee channel, ragging reports to the Anti-Ragging Committee with the national helpline shown, and distress to the counseling center.

uses.title: Semester results and grade cards
uses.description: Grade cards released behind secure links once the examination controller publishes results, with revaluation and supplementary exam windows in the same notice.

uses.title: Alumni network and mentoring
uses.description: An opt-in alumni directory, annual profile refresh, event invitations by batch and city, and mentor matches between alumni and current students approved by the alumni office.

kpis: Helpdesk questions answered with a cited source
Refunds processed within the policy timeline
Alumni profiles confirmed in the last year
systems: College ERP such as Samarth eGov or MasterSoft
LMS such as Moodle or Canvas
DigiLocker and Academic Bank of Credits

segments.name: Coaching & test-prep institutes
segments.headline: From demo class to results day, with honest claims and attentive mentors
segments.summary: Coaching and test-prep institutes win students in short, intense seasons and keep them through months of tests and doubts. We automate demo-to-enrollment follow-up, batch schedules, attendance alerts to parents, test analytics and doubt routing, designed around the Ministry of Education coaching guidelines and the consumer authority's advertising rules.
challenges: Seminar and ad leads pile up on counselors' phones, demo attendees are not followed up, and each counselor explains fees and refunds differently.
Batch changes, faculty absences and extra classes are announced in large groups that students mute, so classes and tests are missed.
Mock test results show marks and ranks but not why a student is struggling, and doubts sent by photo wait days or reach the wrong faculty.
Advertising and results claims face consumer authority scrutiny, and state coaching laws add registration, refund and student well-being duties.

uses.title: Demo class to enrollment
uses.description: Demo slots booked from ads and seminars, attendance recorded, a counselor call with demo feedback, and the fee plan and refund policy sent in writing before any payment.

uses.title: Batch allocation and change notices
uses.description: Students placed by course, medium, center and timing within capacity, and every schedule change sent only to the affected batch and, for minors, their parents.

uses.title: Attendance alerts to parents
uses.description: Absence from a class or test notifies the parent of a student under eighteen the same day, and repeated absence goes to the student's mentor for a conversation.

uses.title: Faculty absence cover
uses.description: When a faculty member is absent, the coordinator gets a proposed substitute or reschedule and approves the notice before it reaches the batch.

uses.title: Topic-level test analytics
uses.description: Each mock test produces a private topic and time analysis against the student's own history, shared with the student and parent, with mentors alerted to sharp drops.

uses.title: Doubt routing to faculty
uses.description: Doubts sent as photos or text are tagged by subject and chapter and queued to the right faculty, with similar solved questions from your own bank attached.

kpis: Mentor reviews after a sharp score drop
Refunds settled within the published policy
systems: Coaching ERP or app such as Classplus or Teachmint
Online test platform or OMR scanning software
Accounting such as Tally or Zoho Books

segments.name: EdTech & online learning
segments.headline: Turn trials into learners who finish what they start
segments.summary: Online learning businesses live on activation, completion and renewal, often with learners under eighteen. We build product analytics, lifecycle messaging, cohort scheduling and grounded support that respect age gates and parental consent, so adult learners get timely nudges, children are not profiled or targeted, and mentors see who needs a person.
challenges: Many sign-ups never finish the first lesson, and generic email sequences treat a curious visitor and a committed learner the same way.
Completion drops after the first modules, and live cohorts lose attendance when reminders arrive at the wrong time or on the wrong channel.
Learners under eighteen need verifiable parental consent, and from May 2027 the DPDP Act bars tracking, behavioral monitoring and targeted ads aimed at them unless an exemption applies.
Support teams answer the same login, payment, certificate and refund questions all day, while real learning problems wait.

uses.title: Activation-led trial journeys
uses.description: Trial users guided to the first lesson, first quiz and first live session, with nudges based on the step they have not reached, for adult learners who opted in.

uses.title: Age gate and parent consent
uses.description: Sign-up asks for age, routes under-18 accounts to a parent consent step, and switches off behavioral nudges and ad audiences for those accounts.

uses.title: Cohort scheduling and session reminders
uses.description: Learners placed in live cohorts by time zone, language and timing, with session reminders and recordings sent on the channel each learner chose.

uses.title: Completion and re-engagement
uses.description: Learners who stall get one reminder tied to their next module, and those who stay inactive are flagged to a mentor instead of receiving more messages.

uses.title: Grounded learner support
uses.description: Login, billing, certificate and refund questions answered from the help center with citations, and learning or well-being concerns handed to a person.

uses.title: Practice analytics and doubt queues
uses.description: Quiz and test results summarized by topic for each learner, with doubts queued to subject experts and AI-drafted hints reviewed by them before release.

kpis: Refund rate in the first billing cycle
systems: Course platform such as Graphy or an in-house app
LMS such as Moodle for institutional customers
Live class tools such as Zoom or Google Meet
Payment gateway or app store billing
Help center and ticketing such as Freshdesk

automations.title: Admissions enquiries, counselor follow-up and campus tours
automations.summary: Enquiries from ads, the website, fairs, walk-ins and WhatsApp land in one CRM with their source, get an approved acknowledgment and a named counselor, and move to a campus tour or open-day slot with reminders and post-visit follow-up.
automations.problem: In admission season, enquiries arrive faster than the front office can return calls. Leads sit in counselors' personal phones and spreadsheets, families who asked for a tour never get a slot, and the institution cannot tell which campaign or fair produced confirmed admissions.
automations.trigger: A parent or applicant submits a Meta or Google lead form or the website form, scans a fair or walk-in QR code, or messages the admissions WhatsApp number.
steps: Create or update one CRM record per family, de-duplicated by phone number, with source, campaign, grade or program, campus, and the consent and notice version shown on the form.
Send an approved WhatsApp acknowledgment with the prospectus link and the counselor's name, assigned by grade or program, campus and preferred language.
Answer common questions on fees, transport, dates and eligibility only from the approved prospectus and fee schedule; route anything else to the counselor with a short summary.
Offer campus tour and open-day slots from the admissions calendar, share directions and a visitor pass for the gate, and remind the family the day before with a one-tap reschedule.
After the visit, prompt the counselor to record the outcome and send the registration or application link the family asked for.
Escalate enquiries with no counselor contact within the agreed time to the admissions head, and report enquiries, tours and admissions by source each morning.
automations.humanCheckpoint: Counselors make every follow-up call and record outcomes, and the admissions head approves templates, answer content and assignment rules. The workflow never screens or ranks children or parents, and seats under RTE Section 12(1)(c) follow the state's own portal and process.
systems: School or college ERP admission module
automations.data: Collects the enquirer's name, phone, grade or program and source. For K-12 the enquirer is the parent, and child details wait for the application. Consent and notice version are stored with the record, campaigns target parents and adult applicants only, and enquiries that do not lead to admission are deleted after the retention period the institution sets.
kpis: Enquiries with no follow-up after the agreed time
Media cost per confirmed admission by source
outputs: Unified admissions CRM with source tracking
Approved WhatsApp templates and answer library
Campus tour and open-day booking with reminders

automations.title: Demo class to enrollment for coaching institutes
automations.summary: Leads from ads, school seminars and walk-ins book a demo class, get reminders and, after attending, a counselor call informed by their demo feedback. The fee plan, installment schedule, refund policy and batch options go out in writing before any payment.
automations.problem: Coaching admissions peak around board results and entrance exam calendars. Demo attendees are not followed up consistently, counselors explain fees and refunds differently, and pressure tactics or rank promises in follow-up messages now attract consumer authority action.
automations.trigger: An aspirant or parent submits an ad or seminar form, walks in, or messages the institute about a course or demo class.
steps: Record the lead with course, target exam, class, center and source, and check the institute's minimum age and eligibility rules before offering a demo.
Offer demo slots by course and center, send an approved confirmation with timing and address, and remind the aspirant and, for minors, the parent before the class.
Mark demo attendance from the faculty's register or app, and send a two-question feedback form after the class.
Create a counselor task with the feedback and preferred batch timing; the counselor calls to discuss fit and preparation, never rank or selection promises.
Send the written fee plan, installment schedule, refund policy and batch options from approved templates, with a payment link only after the family confirms.
Report demo bookings, attendance and enrollments by course, center and source, and flag leads waiting more than a day for a call.
automations.humanCheckpoint: Counselors hold every enrollment conversation, and the center head approves any discount or installment change. The academic head and the institute's legal adviser approve all templates so that none promises selections, ranks or assured results.
automations.data: Name, phone, course, class and center. Many aspirants are sixteen or seventeen, so the parent's contact and consent are recorded for minors and messages go to the parent too. Leads of minors are never used to build behavioral ad audiences, and unconverted leads are deleted after the period the institute sets.
kpis: Time from demo to counselor call
Enrollments with written fee and refund terms sent
outputs: Counselor task queue with demo feedback
Approved fee, refund and batch templates

automations.title: Trial activation and paid conversion for online courses
automations.summary: Product events show which trial learners reached their first lesson, quiz or live session. Adult learners who opted in get nudges tied to their next step, under-18 accounts get service messages to the parent only, and the growth team sees conversion by course and channel.
automations.problem: Most trial sign-ups never finish a first lesson, and generic drip emails treat every learner the same. Behavior-based nudges suit adults but cannot be applied to children, and countdown pressure or hard-to-cancel trials are dark patterns under the consumer authority's guidelines.
automations.trigger: A learner starts a free trial or sample course on the website or app, or completes, skips or abandons a key activation step.
steps: Ask for age at sign-up and route under-18 learners to a parent consent step that checks the parent is an adult before the account is activated.
Track activation events such as first lesson, first quiz and first live session for adult accounts, and only the service events the course needs for child accounts.
Send adult learners who opted in an email or WhatsApp nudge tied to the step they have not reached, from approved templates with weekly caps.
For child accounts, send the parent only service messages such as the trial end date, the schedule and how to cancel.
Before the trial ends, show the price, renewal terms and a one-click cancel option, and send a reminder before any first charge.
Report activation and trial-to-paid conversion by course, cohort and channel, with child accounts excluded from every ad audience.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The growth lead approves every sequence, cap and template, and the data protection contact approves the age gate and parent consent flow. Refund and cancellation disputes go to the learner success lead, never to an automated reply.
systems: Payment gateway or app store billing
automations.data: Adults: email, phone, course and activation events, with a separate marketing opt-in. Under-18s: the parent's identity and consent record, with analytics limited to what the service needs and no ad tracking. Event data is kept for the period stated in the privacy notice, and learners can withdraw consent or delete their account in settings.
kpis: Cancellations in the first billing cycle
outputs: Activation event plan and analytics dashboard
Age gate and parent consent flow
Approved lifecycle sequences with frequency caps

automations.title: Applications, document checklists and verification for colleges
automations.summary: Applicants complete one form with a program and category checklist. Uploads are checked for completeness, readability and name or date mismatches, the admissions office verifies each file in a queue, and missing items trigger reminders until the seat is confirmed.
automations.problem: Applications arrive across counseling rounds with missing marksheets, blurred category certificates and names that differ between documents. Staff chase applicants by phone, originals are sometimes kept against the rules, and seats stay unconfirmed while the next round approaches.
automations.trigger: An applicant submits the online application, or the admissions office opens a counseling round and invites shortlisted applicants to complete their documents.
steps: Show the checklist for the chosen program and category, such as marksheets, entrance scorecard, transfer and migration certificates, and category or disability certificates.
Check each upload for type, readability and completeness, and extract name, date of birth and marks as a draft to compare across documents.
Place each file in the admissions office queue with mismatches and unreadable pages highlighted beside the original images.
Send polite reminders for missing or rejected items with the reason and deadline, and stop reminders once the file is complete.
Collect the anti-ragging undertaking reference number and the APAAR or ABC ID where applicable, and book an in-person slot to verify and return original certificates.
On approval, send the offer and fee link, write the confirmed student to the college ERP and update seat counts by program and category.
automations.humanCheckpoint: Admissions officers verify every document and decide eligibility, category and seat allocation; extraction only drafts. Originals are verified in person and returned at once, as UGC requires, and withdrawals and refunds follow the UGC fee refund policy with the registrar's approval.
systems: College ERP such as Samarth eGov or MasterSoft
Admissions portal and counseling round lists
DigiLocker and Academic Bank of Credits
automations.data: Marksheets and certificates stay in the institution's own storage with role-based access and never travel over WhatsApp, which carries status updates only. Category and disability documents are visible only to the verifying officers. Extraction runs under enterprise terms without training use, and files of applicants not admitted are deleted after the appeal window.
kpis: Seats confirmed before the next round
outputs: Seat matrix dashboard by program and category

automations.title: Batch and cohort allocation with schedule change notices
automations.summary: New students are placed in batches or live cohorts by course, center or time zone, medium and timing within capacity. Faculty availability is checked, timetables are published, and every later change reaches only the affected students and parents.
automations.problem: Batches fill unevenly, timing preferences live in spreadsheets, and schedule changes are announced in large groups that students mute. In coaching, timings may also need to respect school hours and daily limits under state coaching rules or the institute's own policy.
automations.trigger: A student completes enrollment, a batch reaches capacity, or a coordinator changes a class time, room, faculty member or mode.
steps: Read enrollments with course, center or time zone, medium and preferred timing, and propose placements within room and faculty capacity.
Check proposed timetables against the rules the institute sets, such as no classes during school hours, a weekly off and a maximum daily duration.
Show the plan to the academic coordinator, who adjusts and approves placements and timetables.
Publish each student's batch, timetable and room or joining link in the app, and confirm it to the student and, for minors, the parent.
When a class moves, notify only that batch with a one-tap acknowledgment, and re-send to anyone who has not opened it before the class.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The academic coordinator approves every placement, batch transfer and timetable change, and faculty confirm their availability. Requests to move a student between batches are decided by the academic head, never by the scheduler.
systems: Live class tools such as Zoom or Google Meet
automations.data: Uses name, course, batch, contact numbers and preferred timing. Placement uses course, timing and capacity, not test rankings, and student-facing messages never label batches by performance. Change logs are kept for the academic year to settle disputes, then archived.
outputs: Timetable rule checks agreed with the academic head

automations.title: Absence, late arrival and school bus alerts to parents
automations.summary: Students marked absent without approved leave trigger a private message to the parent by a set time, with reply buttons, and bus boarding, drop and delay updates come from RFID or attendant app events. Unresolved cases reach a staff member who calls the family.
automations.problem: Calling every absent student's family takes a teacher's free period, so calls are late or skipped. Parents of bus students cannot tell whether their child boarded, and the transport office spends the morning answering the same calls.
automations.trigger: The attendance cutoff passes with a student marked absent and no approved leave, or a bus RFID reader or the attendant's app records a boarding, drop or delay.
steps: At the cutoff the institution sets, read attendance from the ERP or biometric system and list students absent without approved leave.
Send the parent an approved utility template with buttons for known reason, arriving late or did not know, and log the reply against the attendance record.
When the parent did not know or has not replied in the agreed time, alert the class teacher or coordinator on a dashboard so a staff member phones the family.
On RFID or attendant app events, notify the parent of boarding and drop, and send route delay notices only after the transport in-charge approves them.
If a child expected at a drop point is not marked off, alert the transport in-charge and the bus attendant at once to resolve by phone.
Show daily absences, late arrivals and unresolved cases, and give counselors a weekly list of repeated absences to follow up personally.
automations.humanCheckpoint: A named staff member phones every family that did not know about an absence, and the transport in-charge handles every missed drop or unusual delay by phone. Absence patterns are reviewed by the counselor or coordinator and never trigger automatic action.
systems: School or coaching ERP attendance module
automations.data: Uses student name, class, attendance status, route and boarding events, sent only to registered parent numbers, and location stays inside the transport system the school controls. Schools stay within the attendance and travel-safety purposes the DPDP Rules allow; coaching institutes rely on recorded parental consent. Boarding logs are deleted after the term.
kpis: Parents notified of unexplained absence by the agreed time
Unresolved absences followed up by phone the same day
Calls to the transport office per day
outputs: Absence alert flow with parent replies
Bus boarding, drop and delay notifications

automations.title: Circulars, homework digests and PTM booking for parents
automations.summary: Teachers post homework and circulars once in the ERP. Parents receive one daily digest per child in their chosen language, acknowledge consent slips with a tap, and book parent-teacher meeting slots from teachers' calendars.
automations.problem: Class WhatsApp groups mix homework, circulars and chatter, expose parents' numbers to each other and leave no record of who read a trip consent slip or a safety notice. PTM scheduling takes days of back-and-forth, and translated circulars depend on whoever has time.
automations.trigger: A teacher or coordinator publishes homework or a circular in the ERP, or the school opens a PTM window for a class.
steps: Collect the day's homework and approved circulars per class and assemble one digest per child at a time the school sets.
Draft translations into the languages parents chose, for a teacher fluent in that language to check before release.
Send the digest on WhatsApp to opted-in parents and through the parent app or email to the rest, with links to attachments instead of files in chat.
Track acknowledgments for circulars that need them, such as trip consent, and remind only the parents who have not responded.
For PTMs, offer slots from each teacher's availability, confirm with the room or video link, and send a reminder on the day.
Report delivery, acknowledgments and PTM attendance by class to the coordinator.
automations.humanCheckpoint: Class teachers approve their digests, a fluent teacher approves each translation, and the principal approves every school-wide circular and any message about safety, discipline or an incident. Parents' replies raising a concern go to the class teacher, not to an automated answer.
automations.data: Uses parent contact, child name, class and section. Parents' numbers are never visible to other parents, and digests carry no marks, health or disciplinary details. Acknowledgments are kept for the academic year as the school's record, and translation drafts run under enterprise terms without training use.
kpis: Teacher time spent on parent messaging
outputs: Daily digest per child with acknowledgments

automations.title: Teacher absence and substitution planner
automations.summary: Leave recorded before a cutoff produces a proposed substitution plan from the timetable, matching free teachers by subject and sharing extra periods fairly. The vice-principal approves it, and substitutes get their periods and lesson notes before the first bell.
automations.problem: Substitutions are worked out on paper before assembly by the one person who knows the timetable. The same willing teachers absorb most extra periods, lesson notes rarely reach the substitute, and in coaching an absent faculty member can leave a batch waiting with no class.
automations.trigger: A teacher records leave in the ERP or HR system, or submits a leave request through the staff form, before the daily cutoff.
steps: Read approved and pending leave for the day and list the periods or batch lectures that need cover.
Find teachers free in each period, preferring the same subject and class, and balance cover using each teacher's load for the week and term.
Show the proposed plan to the vice-principal or academic coordinator, with conflicts and unfilled periods highlighted.
On approval, notify each substitute with class, room and the absent teacher's lesson plan link, and update the display timetable.
In coaching, offer the coordinator a reschedule option for lectures that cannot be covered, and notify the batch once it is approved.
Report substitution load by teacher and term so leadership can see whether cover is shared fairly.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The vice-principal or academic coordinator approves every plan and can override any assignment. Leave approval stays with the principal or HR under the staff leave policy; the planner never approves or rejects leave.
systems: School ERP timetable and leave module
automations.data: Uses staff names, timetables, leave dates and substitution counts, with no medical or personal reasons for leave in the plan. Access is limited to leadership and the timetable coordinator, and load reports are kept for the academic year.
kpis: Spread of substitution load across staff

automations.title: Student and learner helpdesk grounded in the handbook
automations.summary: Students, parents and online learners ask questions on WhatsApp, the portal or the app and get answers cited from the current handbook, fee policy, academic calendar or help center. Grievances, ragging reports and signs of distress go straight to people.
automations.problem: Department offices and support teams answer the same questions about exam forms, hostel rules, scholarships, certificates and refunds all term. Answers vary by who replies, and serious messages about harassment, ragging or distress can sit in the same inbox as routine queries.
automations.trigger: A student, parent or learner sends a question to the helpdesk WhatsApp number, the student portal or the in-app help widget.
steps: Screen every message first for ragging, harassment, self-harm or emergency words agreed with the owner; on a match, alert the named person at once and show the national anti-ragging helpline or Tele-MANAS, 14416.
Classify the rest into topics such as exams, fees, hostel, scholarships, certificates, login or refunds.
Answer only from the approved handbook, policy and help center documents, citing the section used; low-confidence answers are not sent.
Hand grievances to the institution's grievance channel, account-specific requests to the right office, and anything unanswered to a staffed queue with a summary.
Flag questions the documents could not answer so owners can update them, and re-index changed documents the same day.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The dean of students or learner success lead owns the sensitive-message rules and the staffed queue. Ragging reports go to the Anti-Ragging Committee and grievances to the Students' Grievance Redressal Committee; fee waivers, discipline and academic exceptions are decided only by the authorized office.
systems: Student handbook, policies and academic calendar
automations.data: Uses message text, name and student or account ID; the assistant cannot read marks, health or disciplinary records. Sensitive reports are visible only to the designated committee or counselor. Conversations are kept for the period the institution sets, and model calls run under enterprise terms without training use.
kpis: Questions answered with a cited source
Sensitive messages acknowledged by a person within the agreed time
Unanswered questions turned into document updates
outputs: Indexed knowledge base with named document owners
Sensitive-message routing approved by the dean of students

automations.title: Course progress nudges and cohort engagement
automations.summary: Learners who stall get a reminder tied to their next module or live session, cohorts get session and deadline reminders, and learners who stay inactive are flagged to a mentor instead of receiving more messages. Child accounts get parent-facing summaries only.
automations.problem: Completion falls after the first modules, live cohort attendance drops mid-course, and blanket reminder emails get ignored or unsubscribed. Mentors cannot tell which of hundreds of learners need a personal call, and learners under eighteen cannot be profiled for engagement nudges.
automations.trigger: A learner misses a planned module or assignment, a live session or deadline approaches, or an adult learner stays inactive for the period the team sets.
steps: Compute each adult learner's progress against the cohort plan from course platform events, and only completion status for child accounts.
Send live session and assignment deadline reminders on the channel each learner chose, with a weekly message cap.
For adults who stall, send one nudge tied to the next module, with a link back to where they left off.
After repeated inactivity, stop automated nudges and create a mentor task with the learner's progress summary.
Send parents of under-18 learners a weekly progress summary and session schedule, with no behavior-based targeting.
Report completion, attendance and mentor outreach by cohort and course.
automations.humanCheckpoint: Mentors decide whom to call and what support to offer, and the learning lead approves caps and wording. Extensions, deferrals and refunds are decided by the learner success lead under the published policy.
automations.data: Adults: progress events and channel preferences, with opt-in. Under-18s: completion status only, shared with the verified parent, and no engagement scoring. Learners can change channels or stop nudges in settings, and event data follows the retention period in the privacy notice.
kpis: Learners re-engaged after a mentor call
outputs: Progress model based on the cohort plan

automations.title: Test analytics and doubt routing to faculty
automations.summary: Each mock test produces a private topic and time analysis against the student's own history for the student, parent and mentor. Doubts sent as photos or text are tagged by subject and chapter and queued to the right faculty, with similar solved questions attached.
automations.problem: Test results show marks and ranks but not which topics or habits cost marks. Doubts sent by photo in crowded groups wait days or reach the wrong teacher, and mentors notice a struggling student only after several poor tests.
automations.trigger: Results of a mock or practice test are published from the test platform or OMR scanner, or a student submits a doubt in the app, portal or doubt WhatsApp number.
steps: Import question-level responses and compute accuracy and time by subject, chapter and difficulty, compared with the student's previous tests.
Publish a private analysis to the student and, for minors, the parent, with practice sets from the institute's own question bank and no public rank lists.
Alert the student's mentor when scores drop sharply or tests are missed, with the analysis attached for a conversation.
Read submitted doubt photos or text, tag subject, chapter and question type, and attach similar solved questions from the institute's bank.
Queue each doubt to the right faculty or doubt solver with a response target; faculty may start from an AI-drafted hint that they edit before sending.
Report doubt volume, resolution time and recurring weak topics to the academic head for remedial classes.
automations.humanCheckpoint: Faculty answer every doubt and approve any drafted hint before it reaches a student. Mentors decide on counseling or extra classes, and any sign of stress or distress goes to the institute's counselor, never to an automated message.
systems: Online test platform or OMR scanning software
automations.data: Uses responses, scores and doubt submissions for the student's own academic support, with parental consent for minors. Analyses are private to the student, parent and assigned staff, are never used for advertising or behavioral profiling, and are deleted or anonymized after the course ends and the retention period passes.
kpis: Doubts answered by the right subject faculty first time
Mentor reviews after a sharp score drop
Weak topics covered in remedial classes

automations.title: Report cards and results released securely to families
automations.summary: Once the principal or examination controller locks results, each report card or grade card is generated and the parent or adult student is notified with a secure, expiring link. PTM booking or revaluation options follow in the same notice.
automations.problem: Report cards are printed, signed and handed out on one crowded day, or forwarded as PDFs in groups where they can reach the wrong family. Corrections after release are messy, and colleges field calls about grade cards, revaluation windows and supplementary exams.
automations.trigger: The principal or examination controller marks results as final in the ERP or examination system for a class, program or semester.
steps: Generate each student's report or grade card from the locked results using the approved template and the remarks teachers entered.
Check for missing marks, unapproved remarks or records the exam office has flagged, and hold those until the exam office clears them.
Notify the parent or adult student with an approved template and a secure link that opens after a one-time code, never the document in chat.
Include the PTM booking link for schools, or revaluation and supplementary exam windows and fees for colleges.
Log every open, resend on request, and point families to DigiLocker where the board or university issues documents through it.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The principal or examination controller locks results and approves release, and teachers own their remarks. Revaluation, grace marks and any hold on a result are decided only by the examination office under the institution's rules, never by the workflow.
systems: School ERP or examination management system
automations.data: Results stay in the institution's systems behind expiring links with one-time codes, and every open is logged. Notification messages carry no marks. Links expire after the period the institution sets, and documents remain available in the parent app or portal under normal access controls.
kpis: Report cards opened within a week of release
PTM bookings from the release notice
outputs: Report and grade card generation from locked results
Secure link delivery with open logs

automations.title: Respectful fee reminders, payment links and receipts
automations.summary: Fee payers receive courteous reminders before and after due dates with a UPI payment link, receipts arrive instantly, and installment, concession or refund requests go to the accounts office. Reminders never reach children, class groups or noticeboards.
automations.problem: Accounts staff chase dues by phone, reminders sometimes reach the wrong parent or a class group, and children can be embarrassed when dues are raised in class. Installment and refund requests get lost between the front office and accounts, and receipts are issued by hand.
automations.trigger: A fee installment approaches or passes its due date in the ERP fee ledger, a payment succeeds or fails at the gateway, or a fee payer asks about fees.
steps: Read due dates, amounts and concessions from the ERP fee ledger and send an approved reminder to the registered fee payer a set number of days before the due date.
Include a payment link for UPI, cards and net banking, and post successful payments to the ledger with an instant receipt, or a GST invoice where the fee is taxable.
After the due date, send no more than the agreed number of courteous reminders, each with an option to request an installment plan or speak to accounts.
Route installment, concession, scholarship and refund requests to the accounts officer with the student's ledger summary and the applicable refund policy.
Give accounts a daily view of dues, promises to pay and failed payments, with no list shared with teachers or classes.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The accounts officer decides installment plans, concessions and refunds, and the principal or registrar approves reminder wording and frequency. Any step that affects a student's classes, exams or results is a management decision under the institution's policy and the law, never automated.
systems: School, college or coaching ERP fee module
Payment gateway such as Razorpay or PayU
Accounting such as Tally or Zoho Books
automations.data: Uses fee payer contact, student name, class and amounts due, sent only to the registered fee payer. Messages state amounts and links, never compare students or threaten consequences. Payment records follow accounting retention rules, and reminder logs are kept for the academic year.
kpis: Installment requests resolved within the agreed time
Refunds paid within the published timeline
outputs: Approved reminder sequence with frequency caps

automations.title: Alumni directory, events and mentoring
automations.summary: Graduating students opt in to the alumni network, profiles are refreshed by a short annual form, event invitations go to relevant batches and cities, and mentor matches between alumni and current students are approved by the alumni office.
automations.problem: Alumni records go stale within a few years of graduation, invitations go to dead email addresses, and mentoring and placement referrals depend on a few personal networks. Reunions and giving drives are organized from scratch each time.
automations.trigger: A student graduates and is invited to join, an annual profile refresh falls due, or the alumni office schedules an event, mentoring round or giving campaign.
steps: Invite graduating students to opt in with a consent screen that states how their details will be used and what other alumni can see.
Send an annual refresh form for employer, city and mentoring interests, and mark records that bounce or stay unconfirmed.
Segment invitations by batch, program and city, and track registrations and attendance for each event.
Suggest mentor matches between opted-in alumni and current students by field and interest, for the alumni office to approve and introduce.
Report profile freshness, event attendance and mentoring activity, and acknowledge every gift with a receipt from the accounts office.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The alumni relations officer approves every campaign, introduction and mentor match, and current students choose whether to accept a mentor. Directory details are shown to other alumni only where each person chose to share them.
systems: Alumni records in the college ERP
automations.data: Uses alumni contact, batch, program, employer and interests with opt-in consent that alumni can change or withdraw at any time. A current student's details reach a mentor only after the student agrees. Records that stay unconfirmed after repeated refresh attempts are deleted.
kpis: Alumni profiles confirmed in the last year

systems.role: Source of truth for admissions, attendance, timetables, fees, exams and student records. We read and write through its APIs or approved exports, and the ERP stays the system of record.
Holds courses, assignments, progress and live session links. We use its events and APIs for homework digests, cohort reminders, progress nudges and analytics.
Batch rosters, test responses and solved questions that feed batch scheduling, test analytics and doubt routing.
Generate attendance and boarding events. We consume events from the vendor's interface, and location data stays within the transport system the school controls.

examples: APAAR and Academic Bank of Credits
systems.role: Government rails for student identity, credits, verified documents and anti-ragging undertakings. We record IDs and reference numbers where families consent and the institution participates, and leave issuing to the official platforms.
Payment links, UPI, receipts and reconciliation against the ERP fee ledger, with GST invoices where a fee is taxable.

examples: WhatsApp Business Platform via a solution provider
systems.role: Family channels with their own rules: opt-in and approved templates for WhatsApp, registered headers and templates for SMS, and preference checks for calls.

kpis.name: Enquiry first response time
kpis.definition: Median time from a new admissions enquiry to the first meaningful reply by a counselor or approved automated message, split by staffed and unstaffed hours.
kpis.why: Families enquire with several institutions at once, and the first useful answer often decides who gets the visit.

kpis.name: Enquiry-to-enrollment conversion
kpis.definition: Share of enquiries in a season that become confirmed admissions or paid enrollments, by source, program and campus.
kpis.why: Shows which channels and counseling practices actually fill seats, not just generate leads.

kpis.name: Media cost per confirmed admission
kpis.definition: Media spend for a campaign divided by the confirmed admissions or enrollments attributed to it in the CRM, for the same season.
kpis.why: Moves marketing reviews from cost per lead to cost per seat filled.

kpis.name: Unexplained absence notification time
kpis.definition: Time from the attendance cutoff to the parent being notified of an absence without approved leave, plus the share of unresolved cases phoned by staff the same day.
kpis.why: A child safety measure that parents and school leaders care about most.

kpis.name: Circular acknowledgment rate
kpis.definition: Share of parents who acknowledged a circular that requires it, such as a trip consent slip, by its deadline.
kpis.why: Shows whether important notices are received and read, not just sent.

kpis.name: Teacher time on administration
kpis.definition: Estimated weekly hours teachers and coordinators spend on substitution planning, parent messaging and report card handling, sampled before and after launch.
kpis.why: The purpose of staff-side automation is time returned to teaching and preparation.

kpis.name: On-time fee collection
kpis.definition: Share of fee installments paid by the due date or within the grace period, by class, program or batch.
kpis.why: Tests whether private reminders and easy payment work without pressure on families or children.

kpis.name: Doubt resolution time
kpis.definition: Median time from a doubt being submitted to an answer from the assigned faculty, by subject and batch.
kpis.why: Unanswered doubts are a common reason coaching and online learners fall behind.

kpis.name: Course completion rate
kpis.definition: Share of enrolled learners who complete the required modules of a course or cohort within the planned period.
kpis.why: The core outcome for online learning and a strong driver of renewals and referrals.

kpis.name: Human handoff rate
kpis.definition: Share of helpdesk conversations transferred to staff under the agreed rules, by reason such as grievance, sensitive message or low confidence.
kpis.why: Confirms sensitive matters reach people and shows where knowledge content needs work.

governance: Parents first: an under-18 learner's data is processed only with recorded, verifiable parental consent or under an exemption that clearly applies, and messages about a child go only to registered parent numbers.
No automated decisions about students: AI may draft, classify, extract and summarize, but admissions, grades, concessions, discipline and refunds stay with the authorized staff member.
No profiling or targeting of children: behavioral nudges and ad audiences are built only from adults who opted in, and child accounts are excluded from both.
Sensitive-message testing on every change: a ragging, harassment, distress and emergency script approved by the principal or dean of students runs before each release of templates, rules or prompts.
Minimum data in messages: notifications carry no marks, health, disciplinary or fee comparisons, and documents open only behind expiring links with one-time codes.

Role-based access, processing logs kept at least one year as the DPDP Rules require, quarterly access reviews, AI providers under enterprise terms without training on student data, and a breach runbook for informing families and the Board.

compliance.title: DPDP Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025 on children's data
compliance.description: Anyone under eighteen is a child. Before processing a child's data, institutions need verifiable consent from a parent confirmed as an adult, and may not track, behaviorally monitor or target ads at children. The Rules lift these limits for educational institutions only for tracking needed for educational activities or the safety of enrolled children, and for school transport providers only for location during travel. These duties apply from May 2027; we design for them now.

compliance.title: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act 2009
compliance.description: In admissions covered by the Act, Section 13 bars capitation fees and any screening of a child or parents other than random selection, and Section 12(1)(c) requires private unaided schools to admit at least a quarter of their entry class from disadvantaged groups and weaker sections, through the state's process. Our admissions workflows never score or rank children or parents, and leave these seats to the state portal.

compliance.title: Ministry of Education Guidelines for Regulation of Coaching Center, 2024
compliance.description: Circulated to states in January 2024 for adoption through their own laws, the guidelines expect registration, a website listing tutor qualifications, courses, fees and refund policy, no misleading promises of ranks or marks, a minimum enrollment age of sixteen, pro-rata refunds when a student leaves mid-course, and support for student well-being. Rajasthan and Jharkhand passed coaching laws in 2025, so workflows follow each state's rules.

compliance.title: Consumer rules on coaching advertising and online selling
compliance.description: The Central Consumer Protection Authority's 2024 coaching guidelines, which also cover online coaching, bar false claims about courses, faculty, fees, refunds, success rates and ranks, require a successful candidate's written consent before using their name, photo or testimonial, and require prominent disclosures. Its 2023 dark pattern guidelines list false urgency, subscription traps and drip pricing. Your legal adviser reviews our templates and checkouts against both.

compliance.title: UGC rules on refunds, original certificates, ragging and grievances
compliance.description: UGC's fee refund policy governs refunds when students withdraw, and institutions must verify original certificates and return them immediately rather than retain them. Students and parents file an online anti-ragging undertaking each year, and the 2023 grievance regulations require an online channel, a Students' Grievance Redressal Committee and an Ombudsperson. Our admissions and helpdesk workflows route to these processes.

compliance.title: WhatsApp policy and TRAI rules for family messaging
compliance.description: WhatsApp requires opt-in, approved templates outside the 24-hour customer service window and a clear route to a person. SMS and calls in India follow TRAI's TCCCPR: registered DLT headers and templates, separate promotional and service categories, an opt-out in promotional messages under the 2025 amendment, and no fresh consent request for ninety days after a customer opts out.

faqs.question: Will an AI chatbot answer parents and students on our behalf?
faqs.answer: Only for routine questions, and only from content your team approves, such as the prospectus, fee schedule, handbook or help center, with a citation to the source. Anything about a specific child's marks, discipline, health or fees, and every grievance, ragging report or sign of distress, goes to a named person. Your principal, dean of students or learner success lead signs off the routing rules and the sensitive-message test script before launch.

faqs.question: Do we need to replace our school ERP, LMS or coaching app?
faqs.answer: No. We connect to the systems you already run through their APIs, vendor integrations or approved exports, and your ERP remains the record for admissions, attendance, fees and results. Where a system offers no interface, we agree a safe interim route such as scheduled exports and state its limits clearly.

faqs.question: Can we keep using class WhatsApp groups?
faqs.answer: You can, but official communication moves to a WhatsApp Business number and the parent app: each parent receives messages individually, numbers are not exposed to other parents, and acknowledgments are recorded. Groups can stay for informal class updates if the school wishes, under its own moderation policy.

faqs.question: How do you handle children's data under the DPDP Act?
faqs.answer: We design for the Act and the DPDP Rules, whose children's provisions apply from May 2027: verifiable parental consent for under-18s, no behavioral tracking or targeted advertising directed at children, and only the narrow educational and safety tracking the Rules permit for schools and their transport providers. Your legal or compliance owner reviews the consent wording. Nothing on this page is legal advice.

faqs.question: Will automated fee reminders upset parents?
faqs.answer: They are designed not to. Reminders go privately to the registered fee payer, use wording your principal or registrar approves, stop after an agreed number, and always offer a way to request an installment plan or speak to accounts. Children, class groups and teachers never see who owes fees.

faqs.question: Can you help a coaching institute keep its advertising and results claims safe?
faqs.answer: We build workflows that keep claims factual: result posts drawn only from candidates who gave written consent after their results, disclosures placed beside every claim, and follow-up templates reviewed by your legal adviser. We do not approve legal claims ourselves, and no message we build promises selections or ranks.

faqs.question: We are an international school or sell courses abroad. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: It can. In the US, COPPA covers online services directed at children under thirteen, and its amended rule has required compliance since April 2026, while FERPA governs education records at institutions funded by the US Department of Education. If you offer services to people in the EU, the GDPR may apply alongside the DPDP Act. We scope these requirements with your legal team during discovery.

faqs.question: How long does a first project take, and what drives the cost?
faqs.answer: A first pilot usually runs three to six weeks, depending mainly on ERP access and template approvals, and we plan admissions work ahead of your season. We quote after discovery, once your systems, volumes and existing licenses are known. Provider charges such as WhatsApp messaging, SMS and model usage are billed by those providers and shown separately.
